html:
The Battle of Salsu was fought in 612 at the Salsu River, probably the Chongchon in today's North Korea, where the Goguryeo general Eulji Mundeok destroyed a huge invading army of the Sui dynasty of China.

Emperor Yang of Sui sent a vast force against Goguryeo. A strike column marched on Pyongyang, but Eulji drew it on with feigned retreats until it was far from its supplies, then attacked as it crossed the river on the way back. Chinese records say only a few thousand of the column returned.

The defeat, and the cost of more failed invasions, helped bring the Sui down in 618. Eulji Mundeok became one of Korea's great heroes, honoured on both sides of the border, and the victory became a symbol of Korean resistance to China. Goguryeo was finally destroyed by the Tang and Silla in 668.
